prompt: A manufacturer has $5M in capex approved this year across 3 plants and 4 candidate upgrade projects, only some of which fit the budget. Recommend which to fund.
context: Projects: (1) Plant A line-speed upgrade — $2.2M cost, projected $1.1M/year margin improvement, 2-year payback. (2) Plant B safety-compliance retrofit — $1.4M cost, required by an updated safety regulation with a 9-month compliance deadline, no direct revenue impact. (3) Plant C energy-efficiency retrofit — $1.8M cost, projected $450K/year savings, 4-year payback, eligible for a government efficiency rebate covering 20% of cost. (4) Plant A warehouse automation — $2.6M cost, projected $700K/year savings, 3.7-year payback. Total capex budget: $5.0M.

binaryCriteria.description: Funds the safety-compliance retrofit regardless of its payback profile, because of the regulatory deadline.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if the compliance retrofit is deprioritized below a better-payback discretionary project.

binaryCriteria.description: The recommended combination of funded projects totals at or under the $5.0M capex budget.
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if all 4 projects are recommended for this year without acknowledging the budget shortfall.

binaryCriteria.description: Explicitly names which project(s) are deferred to a future period and gives a reason (e.g., budget exhausted after compliance + best-payback project).
binaryCriteria.guidance: Fail if a deferred project is simply omitted without explanation.

goldNotes: A strong answer treats the safety-compliance retrofit ($1.4M) as mandatory given the regulatory deadline, regardless of its payback economics, leaving $3.6M of the $5.0M budget for the remaining 3 projects. Among those, the line-speed upgrade ($2.2M, 2-year payback) is the best economics; combined with the compliance retrofit that is $3.6M, leaving only $400K — not enough for either the energy retrofit ($1.8M net of a 20% rebate, i.e. effectively ~$1.44M) or warehouse automation ($2.6M). A rigorous answer should note this and recommend funding compliance + line-speed upgrade this year ($3.6M total), explicitly deferring energy-efficiency and warehouse automation to next year (possibly re-checking rebate eligibility timing for the energy project), rather than trying to squeeze all 4 projects into $5M or ignoring the compliance deadline.
